findings.one_line: The load-bearing bound (8) is asserted rather than derived from the scalar resolvent: its Hoeffding argument omits the explicit diagonal third-and-higher contractions (notably nonzero conditional third-moment terms) and gives no coefficient calculation establishing the claimed sqrt(n)/psi_*^2 bound for them; consequently (10), and hence the native aggregate remainder used downstream, is not discharged.

The passage from singular-space perturbations (1)--(3) to the aggregate Hessian bound (5) and relative three-block weight inequality (9) supplies no expansion of the fitted coefficients or termwise control; these are precisely the native plug-in terms needed for |Bhat_2-B_2|=o(s) and Vhat/s^2->1, so the asserted rates cannot be reproduced from the declared dependencies.

In the common-adoption specialization the note has g asymp n, whereas the supplied Choi--Yuan condition (iii) for its adoption group has |G_1| sqrt(n log n)=o(n^(3/2)); this fails when |G_1|=g asymp n, so the claimed one-date intersection reduction needs a nonempty compatible subclass (or must be rescaled).

The conditional exponential-moment assumption implies this unconditional psi_2 bound with the same K by iterated expectation; every listed consumer also assumes the conditional version, so this separate class restriction is inert.
Balanced growth, m>=c_S n, and max S<min W already imply H<=T-m<=(1-c_S/C)T; the separately imposed fixed gap from T does not broaden any reproduced result.
